pyeto.description: The full calculation, from your own weather sensors: temperature, humidity, pressure, wind and solar radiation. The most accurate option, and the one that asks for the most.

static.description: A fixed amount of evaporation per day, which you set yourself. No sensors and no weather service.

passthrough.description: Takes an evapotranspiration figure that already exists, from a sensor or from a weather service that publishes one. The recommended path when you have one.

setup.title: Setup
setup.description: A guided way to create your first zone. It asks one question at a time, and only the questions your previous answers leave open.
setup.failed: Something went wrong and nothing was created. The other tabs are still there if you would rather set it up by hand.

zone.question: What are you watering?
zone.help: One zone is one valve, watering one area.
zone.name: Name
zone.throughput-help: How much water this zone delivers per minute. Measure it if you can, rather than taking it from a datasheet: it is what every duration is derived from, and it is the quietest way to water twice as long as you meant to.

environment.question: Where does it grow?
environment.outdoors-help: Open air. Rain reaches it, and the sky is worth asking about.
environment.under-glass-help: A greenhouse, a polytunnel, a conservatory. No rain arrives, and a forecast describes weather these plants never see.

weather.question: Where should the evaporation figure come from?
weather.service-help: Nothing else to install. Smart Irrigation takes the weather for your location and computes evapotranspiration from it.
weather.no-service-indoors: A weather service is not offered here: it describes the sky, which these plants are not under.
weather.sensors-help: You have sensors for temperature, humidity and the rest. The most accurate option, because it measures where the plants actually are.
weather.et: A sensor that already reports evapotranspiration
weather.et-help: Something else already computes it, and Smart Irrigation should use that figure as it stands.
weather.static-help: No sensors and no service. You give one number and it is used every day. Rough, but it still tracks what you have already watered.
weather.service-help-entity: The current values and the forecast come from your weather entity, and Smart Irrigation computes evapotranspiration from them. The rain comes from a rain sensor of yours, asked for in the next step.

sensors.question: Which entities should it read?
sensors.help: Only the ones the calculation actually uses are asked for.
sensors.help-optional: Fields marked optional can stay empty: missing weather values are estimated, and without a rain sensor no rain is credited.
sensors.suggested-note: Fields marked suggested are filled in from the sensors in your Home Assistant. Check that each is the one you mean.
sensors.lux-hint: Under glass a light sensor can stand in for solar radiation: pick your illuminance entity here and set its source to Light sensor (lux) afterwards, in the sensor group.
sensors.static-question: How much does it evaporate per day?
sensors.static-help: A depth of water, in the unit your zones use. Somewhere around 4 to 5 mm a day is common for a temperate summer.
sensors.rain-help-entity: This weather entity only forecasts rain. Pick a sensor that measures rain for one of these fields: a rate or a gauge total. No rain sensor? Use Open-Meteo instead.

review.question: Ready to create
review.help: This creates a calculation module, a sensor group and a zone, exactly as the other tabs would. Nothing is locked afterwards.

setup.done-note-zone: It appears under Zones, with its sensor group under Sensor groups. Nothing here is special: edit either of them as you would any other.
setup.done-next-static: With a fixed amount per day it needs no readings: the next calculation works out what it is short of.
setup.done-next-service: Its weather comes from the weather service, its duration with the first calculation. Calculate now fetches the weather and calculates the zone at once.
setup.done-next-sensors: Its duration comes with the first calculation. Calculate now reads your sensors and calculates the zone at once.
setup.calc-duration: Calculated: it waters {duration} at the next start.
setup.calc-nothing: Calculated: it is not short of water yet.
setup.calc-failed: The calculation did not work. The zone says why under Zones.

history.title: History
history.no-data: No data has been retrieved from the weather service yet.

weatherservice.title: Weather service
weatherservice.description: View and change the weather service used to fetch weather data — no need to reinstall the integration. The API key is validated and the change is applied immediately.

labels.ha-weather-entity: A weather entity in Home Assistant

messages.no-service: No weather service is used — weather data comes from your own sensors only.
messages.reload-note: Saving validates the API key against the service and applies the change immediately.
messages.owm-onecall-hint: OpenWeatherMap needs the One Call API 3.0 plan (One Call by Call). It is free up to 1000 calls/day but must be activated with a card, and a new key can take up to a couple of hours to work. A plain default key is rejected.
messages.ha-entity-hint: Current values and the forecast come from this entity, solar radiation and reference ET from Open-Meteo. It only forecasts rain: give each sensor group a rain sensor under Current precipitation.
messages.rain-groups-on-service: {count, plural, one {# sensor group still takes its} other {# sensor groups still take their}} rain from the weather service, which reports none: {groups}. Choose a rain sensor under Current precipitation, or the zones are watered after every shower.
messages.reload-note-entity: Saving checks that the entity exists and applies the change immediately.
messages.invalid-entity: Choose a weather entity: this one does not exist any more, or is not a weather entity.

backuprestore.title: Backup / restore
backuprestore.description: Export the full Smart Irrigation configuration to a JSON file, or restore it from a previous backup.

backup.title: Backup
backup.description: Download the complete configuration (general settings, zones, modules and sensor groups) as a JSON file.

restore.title: Restore
restore.description: Load a previously exported JSON file to replace the current configuration.

messages.invalid-file: This file is not a valid Smart Irrigation backup.
messages.confirm-warning: Restoring overwrites all current general settings, zones, modules and sensor groups. This cannot be undone.
messages.reload-note: Restoring replaces everything and reloads the integration to apply the change.

automatic-duration-calculation.description: The watering duration of each zone comes from its water balance: what the weather took out of the soil, minus the rain. Here you choose when it is calculated. What starts the watering is decided elsewhere, by the start trigger.

labels.calc-when-hint: Just before each start: at the start trigger, with the freshest weather, when Smart Irrigation starts the watering. At a fixed time: daily at the time below, when something else starts it and reads the durations (Irrigation Unlimited, a schedule). Only when I ask: by button or service.
labels.calc-time-hint: The daily calculation: the water lost is added to the water balance of each zone and the watering durations are set.
labels.hourly-calculation-hint: Adds up the FAO-56 hourly equation for each hour since the last calculation, instead of the daily one on averages, which hide whether sun and heat came together. Worth it when readings arrive through the day. New installs start on it; older ones keep the daily one until you switch.

errors.warning-update-time-on-or-after-calc-tim: Warning: weather data update time on or after calculation time

automatic-update.description: Collect and store weather data automatically. Weather data is required to calculate zone water balances and durations.

continuousupdates.header: Continuous updates for all sensor groups
continuousupdates.description: For every sensor group below: records each change of a group's sensors, not one reading per update, so the hourly calculation and the rain get finer data. Zones are still calculated on schedule, not at each change. A weather service in the group is still read once per update: no extra requests.

labels.advanced-hint: Shows the settings that tune the model: drainage, thresholds, multiplier, how far ahead a zone looks. They have sound defaults; leave this off unless you know you need them. Your values are kept either way.

setup-assistant.description: Four questions at most, and it creates a sensor group and a zone for you, choosing what each needs. For a first zone, another one, or a fresh start.

iu-import.description: Moving over from Irrigation Unlimited? Bring its zones, sequences and schedules here, with a preview of everything first.

master-switch.title: Smart Irrigation
master-switch.label: Calculate and water
master-switch.description: Off, Smart Irrigation keeps taking its weather readings and keeps its sensors, but calculates nothing, leaves every water balance as it is, opens no valve and runs no program. Switched on again, the time it was off is not counted.
master-switch.off-note: Switched off: nothing is calculated and nothing is watered. The weather readings carry on, and the time it is off will not be counted when it is switched on again.
master-switch.confirm-off: Switch Smart Irrigation off? Whatever is watering stops now, and nothing is calculated or watered until it is switched on again.

sections.calculation-sub: How much each zone needs, and when it is worked out.
sections.control-sub: What opens the valves, and what starts a run.

translate.text: Apart from English and French, the translations of this panel were machine-made and nobody who speaks the language has checked them yet. If a word or a sentence reads oddly in yours, you can correct it in your browser, with no technical knowledge needed.

next-run.title: Next run

labels.no-valve: No valve linked, so not watered

next-run.no-start: No start time could be worked out yet.
next-run.nothing-to-water: Nothing to water: no zone has reached its irrigation threshold.
next-run.main-schedules: Started by the main program's schedules (the start trigger is not used for now)
next-run.accounts-for-duration: counted back so the run finishes then
next-run.sequencing-sequential: one zone at a time, so the total is every zone added up
next-run.estimated: Estimated: the zones are calculated again just before the start.
next-run.sequencing-parallel: all zones at once, so the total is the longest zone
next-run.sub-nothing: No zone is short enough of water yet. The next start would be {start}.
next-run.sub-not-calculated: The zones have no duration until their first calculation, {when}. Calculate all zones under Zones to do it now.
next-run.sub-postponed: You postponed it. It resumes by itself, and nothing is lost: a zone that is short of water still is.
next-run.headline-not-scheduled: A run is owed, and nothing is scheduled to start it
next-run.sub-not-scheduled: The time above is when it would start. No start trigger is armed right now, which happens when the active trigger is disabled or was not registered. Check the trigger under Settings, and if it looks right, a calculation re-arms it.
next-run.sub-no-trigger: Smart Irrigation starts no watering. Choose a start trigger in the settings to have it water.
next-run.sub-no-valve: The zones short of water have no valve linked, so they aren't watered. Link one to each of them.
next-run.sub-no-zones: Smart Irrigation waters zones. The assistant sets up the first one with you.
next-run.sub-off: It keeps taking its weather readings, but calculates nothing and waters nothing until it is switched on again.

decision.title: Will it be skipped?
decision.will-run: Nothing is holding the run back.
decision.preview-note: Evaluated just now. A forecast can still change before the start.
decision.unavailable: The skip conditions could not be evaluated.
decision.last-none: No run has been decided yet.
decision.detail-anyway-deficit: Goes ahead anyway: a zone that would water is {deficit} mm short, more than twice the rain to expect.
decision.detail-anyway-skips: Goes ahead anyway: the forecast already held the run back {days} days in a row.

estimate.title: Where each zone stands now
estimate.note: Estimated by running the calculation on the readings collected since it last ran. Nothing is committed: a zone keeps the value from its last calculation until the next one.
estimate.none: No zone can be estimated yet.

postpone.prompt: Rain the forecast missed, or a reason of your own?

stale.title: A zone is no longer being calculated
stale.body: Its water need is older than the others, so it is watering on old weather. Check that its sensor group still receives data, and look at the log for what the calculation said about it.

running.headline: Watering now
running.paused-until: Until {when}, then it goes on by itself.

auto_calc_off.title: No watering duration is being calculated
auto_calc_off.body: The watering duration is set to "Only when I ask", so the zones' durations never update by themselves. Choose "At a fixed time" or "Just before each start" under Settings, or calculate by hand when you want a run.

no_automatic_zone.title: No zone waters on its own
no_automatic_zone.body: Every zone is manual or disabled, so a start reaches nothing. Set a zone to automatic for it to be watered by the schedule.

no_valve_path.title: Nothing here opens a valve
no_valve_path.body: Smart Irrigation calculates how long to water; something has to act on it. Either turn on direct valve control under Settings and then link a valve to each zone, or write an automation on the start event (the blueprints do this for you). If an automation already does it, there is nothing to change.

errors.cannot-delete-mapping-because-zones-use-: You cannot delete this sensor group because there is at least one zone using it.
errors.source_does_not_exist: Source does not exist. Please enter a valid source, such as 'sensor.mysensor'.

mapping.hidden_sources: {n} reading(s) not asked: the evapotranspiration is given ready-made, they would only serve to recalculate it.
mapping.et_ignored: Calculated from the weather, so they do not read this evapotranspiration: {zones}. Set them to provided by a sensor or a service on the zone.
mapping.et_missing: Expecting a ready-made evapotranspiration: {zones}. Choose a source for it above.
mapping.et_unused: Not used: every zone of this group is calculated by Smart Irrigation, which works the evapotranspiration out from the other readings. Set a zone to provided by a sensor or a service to give a ready-made value here.
mapping.et_needed: A ready-made value is needed here: the zones of this group are set to provided by a sensor or a service, so None is not offered.

hints.temperature: Air temperature, in the shade. The day's minimum and maximum are taken from it.
hints.dewpoint: The temperature at which the air would be saturated, which tells how much vapour it holds. The weather service is fine here.
hints.humidity: Relative humidity of the air. Dry air draws more water out of the plants.
hints.pressure: Atmospheric pressure. It changes the result very little: the weather service is enough.
hints.windspeed: Wind carries the humidity away from the leaves. Under glass, set a fixed value near 0.
hints.solar radiation: The energy of the sun, the main driver of evaporation. Without it the calculation estimates it from the day's temperature range. Under glass, use a radiation sensor or a light sensor.
hints.precipitation: Rain that fell, as a total, from a rain gauge of your own that adds up. With a weather service, leave it on None.
hints.current precipitation: Rain falling now, as a rate. The weather service provides it; a rain sensor of your own is more precise.
hints.evapotranspiration: The water the plants lost (ET0), already calculated by your sensor or service. Read only by zones set to provided by a sensor or service; a zone Smart Irrigation calculates takes the weather inputs instead.

sources.weather_service_et: Ready-made ET₀ from the weather service

mapping.greenhouse_description: Under glass or plastic: a greenhouse, a polytunnel. No rain reaches it, so precipitation is left out and its fields are hidden. Set two things yourself: Wind speed to a static value near 0, as the calculation assumes open air, and a light sensor for Solar radiation, as the glazing filters the sky.
mapping.module_description: This group only offers the sources this module reads. The zones using it inherit the choice.
mapping.module_undecided: No module chosen yet, so every source is offered and each zone using this group keeps its own. Pick one to see only the sources it reads.
mapping.rain_not_from_entity: The weather entity reports no rain that fell, only a forecast: choose a rain sensor here, or the zones are watered after every shower.
mapping.rain_hint_entity: Rain falling now, as a rate. The weather entity only forecasts it: choose a sensor that measures rain.

actions.assistant: Set it up with the assistant

zone-actions.reset-hint: These two discard data of every zone. Each asks first.

zones.description: Specify one or more irrigation zones here. The irrigation duration is calculated per zone, depending on size, throughput, state, module and sensor group.

labels.name: Name
labels.input-method-hint: How the water delivered is known: from the area and the flow of the zone, or directly as a precipitation rate if you have measured it.
labels.state-hint: Automatic: Smart Irrigation calculates the duration from the water balance and waters at the start. Manual: it waters the duration you set, at every start. Disabled: never watered, and its balance is not followed.
labels.mapping-hint: The group of sensors this zone reads its weather from: a weather service, your own sensors, or both.
labels.bucket-hint: The water balance of the zone. Negative: it is short of water. Zero: it has what it needs. Watering brings it back to zero.
labels.maximum-bucket-hint: The most water the soil is taken to hold. A positive balance never goes above it: the surplus is lost.
labels.irrigation-threshold-hint: The deficit from which the zone is watered. Under it, the zone is left alone and the deficit rolls over to the next calculation.
labels.drainage_rate-hint: How fast the soil lets surplus water go. Leave the default if you do not know your soil: 0 means the surplus never drains.
labels.linked-entity-hint: The valve or switch that waters this zone. With direct valve control, Smart Irrigation opens and closes it. With observed watering, every run of it (by hand, an automation or Smart Irrigation) credits the water balance from run time and throughput.
labels.valve-off: A valve can be linked once direct valve control or observed watering is on.
labels.measured-flow-help: Over several runs the zone's flow meter measured a flow that differs from the one set above. It is advice, never applied on its own.
labels.extra-valves-hint: opened and closed together with it
labels.flow-sensor-hint: For exact crediting instead of throughput x time: a cumulative water-meter total (state class total_increasing), not an instant flow rate. The unit is read automatically (L, mL, m³, gal, ft³).
labels.confirm-timeout: Wait for the valve to confirm
labels.confirm-timeout-help: How long the valve has to report that it opened or closed, and how often the open is resent meanwhile. Empty: 8 s, no resend (full controller: 30 s, two); closing 5 s, always tried twice. Cloud valves such as Gardena: wait longer, 0 resends, each command counts against a quota.
labels.safety-off-mode-auto: Automatic (MQTT topic, or a Sonoff SWV on ZHA)
labels.safety-off-mode-help: Automatic: the MQTT topic above if set, or a Sonoff SWV on ZHA. ZHA timed off: any ZHA valve, with the standard timed-off command, untested beyond the SWV. Off: no hardware dead-man for this zone.
labels.safety-off-topic-help: Optional hardware dead-man: the valve device's MQTT set topic (e.g. zigbee2mqtt/my_valve/set). Smart Irrigation sends "on with timed off", so the device closes by itself if Home Assistant stops mid-run. State key: "state" or "state_l1"…"state_l4". Needs on_time in its firmware: test it.
labels.crop-factor-by-month-help: For a crop whose water use follows its growth: the crop factor (Kc) of each month, January first. A month left empty uses the crop factor above, and all twelve empty is that crop factor all year. Seasonal adjustments still apply on top.
labels.available-water-help: How much water this zone's soil holds for the plants, in mm: root depth in metres times what the soil holds per metre (FAO-56: sand 50–110, loam 130–180, clay 120–200). The deficit never exceeds it, and past the allowed share (50% by default) the plants draw less. Empty: not used.
labels.distribution-efficiency-help: The share of the water from the emitters that reaches the plants, in %. Sprinklers in wind or on a slope lose some, drip almost none. Empty: 100%. At 80% a zone waters 25% longer and credits 80% of what it delivers.
labels.days-between-irrigation-help: Empty follows the general setting (Settings, Days between irrigation). A number applies to this zone alone, counted from its last watering: 1 every day if needed, 3 at most every third day, 0 no limit.
labels.soil-moisture-sensor-hint: The zone sits out a run while the soil is at or above the threshold. The water balance is kept.

calculation-method-help.from_weather: From your measurements: temperature, humidity, wind, sun.
calculation-method-help.provided: You already have an evapotranspiration in mm; it is taken as it is.
calculation-method-help.fixed: So many mm a day, whatever the weather.

calculation-methods.provided: Provided by a sensor or a service

labels.forecast-days-help: 0: the zone waters what the weather actually took. 1: tomorrow is taken into account as well, 2: tomorrow and the day after, and so on. The hotter the days ahead, the more is watered today. This is not the rain skip, which is a setting of its own.
labels.engine-shared-help: This setting belongs to this zone alone: each zone has its own, and changing it here changes nothing anywhere else.

soil-types.custom: I set the drainage rate myself

plant-types.custom: I set the crop factor myself

labels.duration-readonly-automatic: Calculated for you: this zone's run comes from its water balance. Set it to manual to type a duration yourself.
labels.duration-readonly-disabled: A disabled zone is never watered, so it has no run time.
labels.et-deficiency-help: What this zone needs per day: ETc, ET0 times the crop factor with the seasonal adjustment, before rain and before scaling to the interval, so it compares across setups. ET0 alone is the zone sensor's `eto` attribute, to check against a weather service.

iu_import.title: Import from Irrigation Unlimited
iu_import.description: Brings your Irrigation Unlimited configuration over: its zones, sequences and schedules become zones, programs and their schedules here. You see everything before anything is changed, and nothing waters until you switch the schedules on.
iu_import.loading: Looking for an Irrigation Unlimited configuration…

source.question: Which configuration?
source.help: Smart Irrigation reads the configuration Home Assistant loads, or the one Irrigation Unlimited's own dialogs keep. You can also paste its YAML.
source.yaml-help: The irrigation_unlimited section Home Assistant loads, with its packages, !include and !secret.
source.entry-help: What Irrigation Unlimited's own dialogs keep.
source.none-found: No Irrigation Unlimited configuration was found. If Irrigation Unlimited is no longer installed and its configuration was in a package, Home Assistant does not load it: paste it below.
source.paste-help: The irrigation_unlimited section, or what is under it. !include, !secret and !env_var are not followed here: write those values out, or import from configuration.yaml.
source.previous: Imported before on {at}. Importing again updates what that import made.
source.unreadable: Home Assistant could not read it:

zones.question: What becomes of each zone?
zones.help: An Irrigation Unlimited zone becomes one of your zones, or a new one. An existing zone keeps its settings and calculation: only what it lacks is filled in.
zones.links: {count, plural, one {# adjust-time automation feeds Irrigation Unlimited from Smart Irrigation: that step is calculated here.} other {# adjust-time automations feed Irrigation Unlimited from Smart Irrigation: those steps are calculated here.}}
zones.creates: A new zone is created, with its valve and pump.

zones.left: No longer in Irrigation Unlimited, left as they are: {zones}.

programs.question: The programs
programs.help: Each sequence becomes a program, and so does a zone with schedules of its own. A sequence whose schedules have different durations becomes one program per duration.
programs.none: This configuration has no schedules to bring over.
programs.schedules-off: Its schedules are switched off until you switch them on.
programs.schedules-stay-on: You switched its schedules on: they stay as they are.
programs.disabled: Switched off in Irrigation Unlimited, and here too.

report.help: Every option of Irrigation Unlimited has a rule. These are the ones that are approximated or left out; everything else comes over as it is.
report.all-carried: Everything comes over as it is.

summary.supplies: Pumps and main valves: {created} new, {updated} updated, {removed} removed

report.nothing-waters: Nothing is watered by the import. Irrigation Unlimited keeps watering until you switch it off and these schedules on.
report.blocked: Resolve what is marked in red first; until then nothing can be imported.
report.full-controller-off: The full controller is off: the programs are imported, but they only water once it is on.

errors.generic: The import did not go through.
errors.changed: The configuration or your zones changed since this preview. Here is what the import would do now: look again, then import.
errors.no_source: No Irrigation Unlimited configuration was found. Paste its YAML.
errors.yaml_unreadable: Home Assistant could not read its configuration.
errors.yaml_invalid: The pasted YAML could not be read.
errors.yaml_not_iu: The pasted YAML is not an Irrigation Unlimited configuration.
errors.unknown_zone: That zone does not exist any more.
errors.zone_not_created: A zone could not be created.
errors.not_ready: Smart Irrigation is not ready yet.
errors.conflicts: Resolve what is marked in red first.
errors.too_big: This is far larger than an Irrigation Unlimited configuration, so it is not read.
errors.not_finite: The configuration holds an infinite value or one that is not a number (.inf or .nan), which Irrigation Unlimited does not have.

done.title: Imported.
done.next: The schedules of new programs are off, so Irrigation Unlimited is still the one watering. Look at the programs, then switch over at the top of this page.
done.next-off: The full controller is off, so these programs do not water yet, and Irrigation Unlimited goes on watering. Switch the full controller on in the settings, then switch over at the top of this page.

conflicts.zone_twice: {zone} and {other} would both become {target}. Choose another zone for one of them.
conflicts.calculated_needs_zone: {zone} is calculated by Smart Irrigation today, from the zone an adjust-time automation feeds it from. Choose that zone or another existing one.
conflicts.program_exists: A program "{name}" ({id}) is in the way: no import made it. Rename or delete it first, in Watering, Programs (with the full controller on).
conflicts.supply_exists: A pump "{name}" ({id}) is in the way: no import made it. Rename or delete it first, in Watering, Pumps and valves (with the full controller on).

iu_import.confirm_remove: This import deletes what an earlier import made and Irrigation Unlimited no longer has: {names}. Go ahead?

cutover.title: Who waters: Irrigation Unlimited or Smart Irrigation
cutover.iu-waters: Irrigation Unlimited waters. The imported schedules are off until you switch over.
cutover.si-waters: Smart Irrigation waters since {at}. Irrigation Unlimited's controllers are off.
cutover.si-waters-now: Smart Irrigation waters: imported schedules are on, and Irrigation Unlimited's controllers are off.
cutover.nobody-waters: Nothing waters: Irrigation Unlimited's controllers are off, and so are the imported schedules.
cutover.both-on: Both would water: Irrigation Unlimited has a controller on, and imported schedules are on too. Switch Irrigation Unlimited off, or the schedules.
cutover.full-controller-off: The full controller is off: switch it on in the settings first, or the imported programs do not water.
cutover.open-programs: Look at them on the Programs page before you switch over
cutover.zones-off: Irrigation Unlimited has these zones switched off and leaves them out of its sequences; here they water with their program: {list}. Switch their step off in the program if they should stay dry.
cutover.iu-not-running: Irrigation Unlimited is not running: there is nothing to switch off.
cutover.confirm-over: Irrigation Unlimited's controllers are switched off, and the schedules Irrigation Unlimited had on are switched on here. From the next schedule on, Smart Irrigation waters. You can go back at any time.
cutover.confirm-back: The imported schedules are switched off, and Irrigation Unlimited's controllers on again. Irrigation Unlimited waters again.

errors.full_controller_off: Switch the full controller on first: without it, nothing waters.
errors.iu_failed: Irrigation Unlimited did not take the switch. What this step had changed is undone: see above who waters.
errors.not_switched: The watering has not been handed to Smart Irrigation, so there is nothing to go back from.
errors.iu_not_running: Irrigation Unlimited is not running: it could not water again. Start it first.

follow-ups.title: What still uses Irrigation Unlimited
follow-ups.help: These automations and scripts name Irrigation Unlimited's services or entities. Once you have switched over, change or remove them: nothing is changed for you.
follow-ups.none: No automation or script uses Irrigation Unlimited.
follow-ups.adjust-time: Hands Irrigation Unlimited a duration Smart Irrigation calculated. After the switch it has nothing to do: the imported steps are calculated here. Remove it.

cutover.left-off: Left off, as Irrigation Unlimited had them switched off: {names}.
cutover.unrecorded: Left off, as the import has no record of which of their schedules Irrigation Unlimited had on: {names}. Switch their schedules on yourself, or go back to Irrigation Unlimited, import again (it records them) and switch over again.

notes.blueprint_zone_gone: a blueprint automation feeds it from zone {zone}, which does not exist any more: it is not taken as calculated
notes.calculated_schedule_durations: calculated durations: the durations of the schedules are not used
notes.check_back_partial: wait {wait, number} s with {resends, plural, one {# resend} other {# resends}}; {lost} not carried
notes.check_back_states: IU does not check this valve; Smart Irrigation always confirms it
notes.cron_days_both: cron {cron}: days of the month and of the week together
notes.cron_expanded: cron {cron} became {count, plural, one {# time schedule} other {# time schedules}}
notes.cron_fields: cron {cron}: a cron expression has five fields
notes.cron_too_many: cron {cron}: more than {max, number} times a day
notes.cron_unreadable: cron {cron}: this cron expression cannot be read
notes.different_bounds: its zones have different bounds; all of them water the longest time
notes.every_limit: every {every, number} days: Smart Irrigation goes up to {max, number}
notes.every_not_number: {value} is not a number of days
notes.feeds_other_zone: an automation feeds it from zone {from}, but it is matched to zone {to}: its calculated duration is that zone's
notes.full_controller_off: the full controller is off: the programs are imported, but they water only once it is on
notes.held_to_limit: {seconds, number} s is held to {limit, number} s, the most Smart Irrigation allows
notes.lead_kept: {time} is kept: moving it earlier by the supply's lead of {lead, number} s would change the day
notes.lead_time: zone "{zone}" has a lead time of {lead, number} s, which Smart Irrigation adds to every fixed run: it waters that much longer than in IU, unless the lead time is set to 0 or the step shortened
notes.no_zone_id: no zone with zone_id {ref} in this controller
notes.not_litres: {value} is not a number of litres
notes.not_options: {value} is not a set of options
notes.off_in_iu_matched: switched off in IU and matched to "{zone}", which stays as it is: the programs leave it out
notes.offset_limit: an offset of {offset, number} min: Smart Irrigation allows {max, number}
notes.offset_rounded: the offset of {seconds, number} s is rounded to {minutes, number} min: Smart Irrigation works in minutes there
notes.one_queue: {count} controllers: their programs run one after the other, as the full controller has one queue
notes.overlap: {count} zones and sequences have schedules: where their runs overlap, IU waters them at the same time, the full controller one after the other
notes.passes_held: {repeats, number} repeats are held to {max, number} passes
notes.period_needs_both: the period {from} to {until} needs both days: the schedule runs all year
notes.rule_entity_states: Smart Irrigation always sends on and off
notes.rule_master_check_back: the confirmation of the master; a supply is not confirmed
notes.rule_master_volume: a meter on the master; Smart Irrigation reads a meter per zone
notes.rule_step_repeat: passes: each a full IU run, but the wait between them is the soak setting, not the step's delay
notes.rule_step_volume: the step's maximum litres: a limit on a timed run, not 'until this volume'
notes.rule_threshold: no 'skip a run shorter than this'; the nearest is a step's minimum deficit, in mm
notes.rule_zone_duration: IU's default for manual runs; water_zone takes a duration of its own
notes.rule_zone_volume: the zone's flow sensor; Smart Irrigation reads its unit, IU's scale factors are not used
notes.seconds_dropped: {time} is taken as {minute}: Smart Irrigation starts on the minute
notes.sun_event: {event}: only sunrise and sunset are known
notes.supply_leads_again: after a wait of {wait, number} s the supply goes off and leads again: the next zone opens up to {lead, number} s later than under IU
notes.supply_stays_on: {seconds, number} s: the supply stays on until the last zone is done
notes.tags_not_followed: {tags} is not followed in pasted YAML: those values were read as the text written. Import from configuration.yaml to have them resolved
notes.tours_held: {repeats, number} repeats are held to {max, number}
notes.unknown_option: not an option Irrigation Unlimited knows
notes.unknown_values_off: {values} is no {option}: the schedule is disabled
notes.wait_held: a wait of {seconds, number} s is held to {held, number} s
notes.zone_no_valve: zone "{zone}" has no valve: it is created, but not watered until one is linked
notes.zone_schedule_duration: a zone's schedule needs a duration: it is not carried

skip.title: Skip on weather
skip.description: A run is held back when one of these checks holds: the rain in the forecast, or the rain, frost and wind measured at its start.
skip.soil-moisture: Soil moisture is set per zone, since each zone has its own sensor.

irrigation_start_triggers.title: Start triggers
irrigation_start_triggers.description: When the watering starts. By default it finishes at sunrise; add a trigger for another moment: sunset, an azimuth or a time, with an offset.
irrigation_start_triggers.active_hint: Only the selected trigger starts the watering, once a day. Default starts so that every zone is done by sunrise; with None, Smart Irrigation starts nothing.
irrigation_start_triggers.usage_before: When a trigger fires, Smart Irrigation emits the event
irrigation_start_triggers.usage_after: — react to it in an automation to start watering. Its data carries trigger_name, trigger_type and offset_minutes, to tell the triggers apart. On a day skipped for rain or for the days between irrigation, no event fires.

name.name: Trigger name
name.description: A descriptive name to identify this trigger

type.name: Trigger type
type.description: The type of solar event to trigger on

enabled.name: Enabled
enabled.description: Whether this trigger is currently active

offset_minutes.name: Before (-) or after (+), in minutes
offset_minutes.description: Minutes before (-) or after (+) the solar event. For sunrise triggers, use 0 for automatic timing based on total zone duration.

azimuth_angle.name: Azimuth angle (degrees)
azimuth_angle.description: Solar azimuth angle in degrees where 0=North, 90=East, 180=South, 270=West

account_for_duration.name: Account for duration
account_for_duration.description: When enabled, irrigation will start early enough to finish at the specified time. When disabled, irrigation will start exactly at the specified time.

dialog.help: When this trigger fires, Smart Irrigation emits the following event — use it in an automation to start watering. The event data includes this trigger's name (and type/offset), so you can react to it specifically:

irrigation_start_triggers.confirm_delete: Are you sure you want to delete the trigger '{name}'?

validation.azimuth_invalid: Azimuth angle must be a valid number
validation.time_invalid: Please enter a valid time as HH:MM.

help.sunrise_offset: For sunrise triggers: Use negative values to start before sunrise, positive to start after. Set to 0 to automatically start early enough to complete all zones before sunrise.
help.sunset_offset: For sunset triggers: Use negative values to start before sunset, positive to start after sunset.
help.azimuth_explanation: Solar azimuth is the compass direction of the sun. 0°=North, 90°=East, 180°=South, 270°=West. You can enter any angle value (e.g., 450° = 90°, -30° = 330°). Use this to trigger irrigation when the sun reaches a specific position.
help.multiple_triggers: You can create several triggers, but only the one selected as active starts irrigation. The others are kept for later.

irrigation_start_triggers.none_selected: No trigger is active: Smart Irrigation starts no watering, whatever the weather. The durations are still calculated; start the watering yourself or from an automation of your own.

seasonal_adjustments.title: Seasonal adjustments
seasonal_adjustments.description: A crop factor and threshold that follow the season, for the months and zones you pick; several in one month multiply. The multiplier scales the zone's crop factor (1 no change, 0.5 half the water), the offset adds to its threshold. A zone can also have a crop factor per month.
seasonal_adjustments.name: Name
seasonal_adjustments.zones_hint: all, or the numbers of the zones, separated by commas.

weather_skip.title: Rain forecast
weather_skip.description: When rain is forecast, Smart Irrigation waters less. This feature requires a weather service to be configured.
weather_skip.threshold_description: Minimum amount of precipitation (in mm) forecasted for today and tomorrow to skip irrigation.
weather_skip.effective_rain_label: Count only rain that reaches the roots
weather_skip.effective_rain_description: Ignore a shower smaller than a fifth of the evapotranspiration of the period: it wets the leaves and evaporates. It is judged on the whole period between two calculations.
weather_skip.forecast_label: Take the forecast rain into account
weather_skip.forecast_description: Below the threshold, each zone gets its deficit less the rain forecast for 24 hours, weighted by its probability: 4 mm forecast against a 10 mm deficit waters 6 mm. At or above it, zones in the open are skipped. Greenhouse zones are not affected.

coordinate_config.title: Location coordinates
coordinate_config.description: Configure location coordinates for weather data retrieval. You can use manual coordinates different from your Home Assistant location if needed.

days_between_irrigation.title: Days between irrigation
days_between_irrigation.description: The fewest days between two waterings of a zone; 0 is no limit. Lawns do well with short intervals, deep-rooted plants with 3 to 7 days and more water per run; 7 fits a once-a-week watering rule. A zone can set its own.
days_between_irrigation.label: Minimum days between irrigation

planning.title: Planning
planning.description: What the programs will water over the next three days. A run the rain may hold back is marked from today's forecast; the weather when it is due decides.
planning.nothing_planned: No program is planned. Add a schedule to a program.
planning.nothing_to_water: Nothing to water for now: no zone of this run is short enough of water.
planning.expected_skipped_precipitation: Expected to be skipped: rain forecast ({mm} mm)
planning.paused_until: Paused until {when}, then the watering goes on by itself.
planning.no_valve: No valve linked, so not watered:
planning.nothing_no_valve: Nothing to water in this run: the zones short of water have no valve linked:
planning.expected_skipped_suspended: Does not run: the program is suspended until {when}

programs.title: Programs
programs.description: A program waters its steps one after the other. A step is one zone, or several watered together, and by default takes the duration Smart Irrigation calculated for it. Several programs never run at the same time: the next one waits its turn.
programs.main_description: Waters every zone, one after the other or together as set below. It is started by the start trigger, or by its own schedules once one is enabled.
programs.adjust_empty: Enter a percentage or seconds to adjust the durations.
programs.sequencing_title: Order of the zones and pauses
programs.confirm_run: Run {name} now? Its valves open straight away.
programs.run_queued: {name} is queued: it starts when what is watering now has finished.
programs.main_schedules_hint: With no enabled schedule, the start trigger set further down this page starts the main program. As soon as one schedule is enabled, the schedules replace that trigger. Its settings are kept, and it comes back if the schedules are disabled or removed.
programs.name: Name
programs.step_zones_help: Zones ticked in the same step are watered at the same time.
programs.step_delay_help: Empty: the program's wait. Negative: the next step starts that long before this one ends.
programs.delay_help: Seconds waited after each step, for line pressure or a slow valve. Negative: each step starts that long before the previous one ends (they overlap).
programs.tours_help: The whole list of steps is watered this many times, each round with its share of the water. Unlike passes, which repeat one step before going on, a round lets each zone soak while the others water.
programs.schedule_anchor: That moment is when the program
programs.schedule_anchor_help: With "must be done", the program starts early enough, from the length of what it has to water, to finish at that moment.
programs.schedule_every_help: Every 3 days with a shift of 0, 1 or 2 lets three programs take turns, one day in three, never on the same day.
programs.schedule_days_of_month_help: Day numbers separated by commas, and "last" for the last day of the month (for example 1, 15, last). A month too short for a day skips it. Empty: any day. It adds to the other filters.
programs.schedule_fallback_time: If there is no sunrise or sunset
programs.schedule_fallback_time_help: For a day without a sunrise or sunset (polar day or night).
programs.schedule_period_help: A period of the year, which may run over New Year (from November to March). Empty: the whole year.
programs.schedule_hard_deadline: Cut the run at the end time
programs.schedule_hard_deadline_help: The run is cut at the end target: the zones that are open are closed and credited for what they watered, and what did not start is skipped.
programs.schedule_conditions_help: What can keep this schedule from watering: rain, frost and wind (Weather, Skip on weather), the days since the last watering (Settings, General) and each zone's soil moisture. Untick what it should ignore, the rain for a greenhouse for example. A postponement you asked for always applies.
programs.schedule_weather_help: Rain, frost, wind, a wet soil and the days you postponed can hold the run back or shorten it. Turn it off for a greenhouse drip line that does not care.
programs.confirm_stop: Stop all watering now? Every valve is closed and the runs under way end.
programs.confirm_delete_program: Delete the program "{name}", with its steps and schedules?
programs.controls_help: For a watering that is under way. Pause closes the valves and holds everything; the rest is watered after the resume. Next step ends the zones the program is on. Stop ends everything.
programs.max_litres_help: A zone of this step stops once its water meter has counted this volume, in litres or gallons as the panel shows volumes. 0: no limit. The meter reports every so often, so the volume is not exact. A zone without a meter ignores it.
programs.run_seconds_help: Optional. Empty: the planned durations. Otherwise the whole program lasts this long, shared between its steps in proportion to their planned durations.
programs.run_replace_help: Off: the program waits for its turn behind what is watering. On: what is watering is stopped cleanly first.
programs.confirm_stop_program: Stop the program "{name}"? Its open zones are closed, or it leaves the queue if it is waiting.
programs.step_bounds_help: Applied in this order: the program's "Adjust durations" percentage, if one is in force (it is set on the program), the time added or removed, then minimum and maximum (0: none). A step that needs no water stays at zero; the minimum never starts it.
programs.min_deficit_mm: Only water when the deficit is at least
programs.min_deficit_mm_help: In mm, 0 to always water. Set, it replaces the zone's own threshold for this step. Fixed-duration steps are always watered.
programs.adjust_help: Makes this program water longer or shorter for the runs that start after it is set. It replaces the previous adjustment. Hours empty: until it is reset.
programs.confirm_reset_adjustment: Remove the adjustment of this program?
programs.main_settings_description: How the main program waters: the zones one after the other or together, the pause between two zones and cycle and soak. Its start trigger is below.
programs.main_schedules_active: For now the main program's schedules start the watering: the start trigger below is not used. It stays editable, and it comes back if those schedules are disabled or removed.
programs.mode_off: The full controller is off. Turn it on in Settings, General.
programs.passes_help: Cycle and soak for this step: its water split into this many passes, each zone soaking between two of them. 1: in a single go.
programs.schedule_fallback_previous: Use the time of the last one seen
programs.main_steps_hint: The main program waters every zone. To water only some of them, or in an order of your own, add one under Other programs below.
programs.conditions_none: No condition is turned on: the rain, frost and wind are set under Weather, Skip on weather, and the days since the last watering under Settings, General.
programs.cond_postponed: the Postpone buttons of the Home page
programs.soak_shared_help: One soak time for every step in passes, in every program and in the main program.
programs.min_over_max: The minimum is above the maximum: the maximum wins, {max}.
programs.confirm_run_replace: Run {name} now? What is watering is stopped first, then its valves open.
programs.run_replacing: What was watering is being stopped; {name} starts straight after.
programs.suspended_until: Suspended until {when}: its schedules do not start it.

supplies.title: Pumps and main valves
supplies.description: A pump or a main valve in front of the zone valves runs while a zone it feeds is being watered. Pick it in each zone's settings.
supplies.name: Name
supplies.delay_before_help: Positive: the pump or main valve comes on this long before the zone valve opens. Negative: the zone valve opens first, and the pump or main valve comes on this long after.
supplies.delay_after_help: Positive: the pump or main valve stays on this long after the zone valve closes. Negative: it goes off this long before the zone valve closes, so a pump never pushes against a closed valve.
supplies.add: Add a pump or main valve
supplies.confirm_delete: Delete "{name}"? The zones that use it will no longer have a pump or main valve.
supplies.kick_seconds_help: For a pump whose pressure controller only starts again after its power has been cut: it is switched off this long, then on, before each start. 0: switched on directly (the default).

observed_watering.title: Observed watering (closed loop)
observed_watering.description: Credits each zone's water balance from real watering, instead of an automation resetting it. Pick a valve or switch per zone under Zones: while it is open, run time times throughput is credited, or the volume a meter measured. Remove set_bucket and reset_bucket calls from your automations, or it counts twice.
observed_watering.direct_control_label: Let Smart Irrigation control the valve
observed_watering.direct_control_description: Smart Irrigation opens each zone's valve, waits the duration and closes it. A valve that can close itself (Sonoff SWV on ZHA, or with an MQTT safety topic) knows the run's length and closes even if Home Assistant fails. Any other keeps watering until Home Assistant is back: give it a hardware time limit.
observed_watering.full_controller_label: Full controller: Smart Irrigation runs all my watering
observed_watering.confirm_full_controller: Turn on the full controller? Smart Irrigation will drive the valves and start the watering itself. A valve found open at startup that no run of ours owns is closed.
observed_watering.full_controller_description: Turns on valve control and adds a Watering tab with programs, planning and pumps. Start trigger, sequencing, pause between zones and cycle and soak move there as the main program and work as before. Off restores the previous behaviour. A valve found open at startup with no run of ours is closed.
observed_watering.sequencing_description: A start trigger that must finish at sunrise works back from it: one after another, from the sum of the run times; all at once, from the longest.
observed_watering.passes_description: Cycle and soak: the same water, split into shorter passes with a pause between them, so heavy soil takes it in instead of letting it run off. One pass waters in a single go, which is the default. A run too short to split is left alone.
observed_watering.pause_between_zones_description: A wait between two zones of a sequential run: time for the line pressure to recover, or for a slow valve to finish closing before the next one opens.
observed_watering.direct_control_locked: The full controller drives the valves: switch it off first to change this.

calculation_log.title: Calculation log
calculation_log.description: Writes every calculation's full input to a file, to compare two similar days that watered very differently: the sensor group's records and how they were combined, the module's intermediates (radiation, ET0), water balance, duration and volume. Off by default; capped and rotated, so it can stay on.
calculation_log.enabled_label: Log calculation inputs to a file
calculation_log.file_hint: Written to config/smart_irrigation/calc_log.jsonl, one JSON record per line. The most recent records are also included in the diagnostics download (coordinates rounded, entity ids removed), so you can attach them to an issue in one step.

blueprints.title: Blueprints
blueprints.install_help: Smart Irrigation copies its example blueprints into your blueprints folder, each one once: a blueprint you delete is not put back. Switch this off to copy none at all; the ones already there are left as they are.

measured_skip.title: Skip on measured conditions
measured_skip.description: Checked at the start of each run, from a sensor or the weather service. A sensor that cannot be read never stops a run.

rain.title: Rain sensor
rain.description: Skip the run while a rain sensor says it is raining.
rain.sensor-hint: A binary sensor that is on while it rains.
rain.history-description: For zones with no rain in mm at all. The sensor's last five days shorten the run, recent ones more: a full day of rain today takes all of it, four days ago a tenth. The water balance is untouched, so the deficit stays. Needs a sensor that stays on while it rains, not one that pulses per tip.

freeze.title: Freeze
freeze.description: Skip the run when the temperature is at or below the threshold.
freeze.sensor-hint: Empty: the weather service's current temperature.

wind.title: Wind
wind.description: Skip the run when the wind is at or above the threshold: a sprinkler in strong wind waters the path, not the bed.
wind.sensor-hint: Empty: the weather service's current wind, at 10 m.

source.service: Reads the current value of the weather service.
source.nothing: No sensor and no weather service: this check holds nothing back.
source.same: The same source as the sensor group {groups}, for the evaporation.
source.other: For the evaporation, the sensor groups read this value elsewhere: {groups}.

card.no_zones: No zones yet. Open the Smart Irrigation panel to add one.
card.live_since: Estimated now, from the readings since {when}

editor.title: Title
editor.compact: Only the zones that would water

confirm.delete_zone: Delete the zone "{name}"? Its settings and water balance are lost.
confirm.delete_mapping: Delete the sensor group "{name}"? The zones that use it will have no weather data.
confirm.delete_module: Delete the module "{name}"? The zones that use it can no longer be calculated.
confirm.reset_bucket: Set the water balance of "{name}" back to zero?
confirm.reset_all_buckets: Set the water balance of every zone back to zero?
confirm.clear_all_weather: Clear all the weather data collected? The next calculation only has the readings that come after.
